Round 1 fresh open critique of issue 99. Id ceiling 5838828591 inclusive. Dispatch SHA `aea1e77017962e2e7186ef64ad8d7e82329da77b`. Process-only; dest unread for product edits.

## Re-verification of P1

The Stop 1 pain holds at the pinned tree.

- Module 6 Part B (`curriculum/modules/06-creating-well-shaped-work.md` lines 367–384) requires a schema-0.8 proposed-scope artifact with one story ID and title, `plan.status: proposed`, two to five `plan.items[].narrative.Acceptance` strings, expected evidence and a trace per criterion, and the no-authority sentence.
- Module 4 cards (`curriculum/modules/04-xbrief-as-durable-state.md` lines 249–251) are "complete facts for a classification exercise, not complete JSON files." The only JSON fence in `curriculum/modules/` is the Module 2 package pin. Lab 5's `PROJECT-DEFINITION` has `"items": []`.
- Recovery row at Module 6 line 524 still says "Compare your item narrative with the worked solution."
- The explained solution JSON introduces item `"status": "proposed"`, `"effort"`, and `plan.metadata.kind` / `swarm` fields the modules never showed.

`scripts/verify-module-6.mjs` already locks the solution to exactly one schema-0.8 proposed JSON with two to five items, each carrying string `narrative.Acceptance` and `narrative.Traces`. That lock is why the answer key can be a complete specimen while the lesson still has no pre-solution shape.

## Inventory (existing mechanisms)

Throwaway 0.119.5 `xbrief:verify -- --format json --style scope --project-root <lab>` (the Lab 7 Task 5 command) against synthetic files:

| Shape | exit |
| --- | --- |
| Solution JSON (effort + kind/story + swarm `needs_refinement`) | 0 |
| Learner first attempt from the issue (`plan.id`, item `status: pending`, `narrative.Evidence` + `Traces`) | 0 |
| Issue-body "minimal" (envelope + one item with `Acceptance` only) | 0 |
| Schema spine only (`xBRIEFInfo` + `plan.title`/`status`/`items: []`) | 0 |
| One item with `title`+`status` and no `narrative` | 0 |
| Lab 7 `story()` helper (empty `items`, `metadata.kind: story`, no swarm) | 0 |
| `xbrief:create --style scope` default (`status: draft`, empty `items`, `metadata.kind: scope`) | 0 |
| Missing `plan.id` | 0 |
| `xBRIEFInfo.version: "0.6"` | 0 |
| `plan.status: running` | 0 |
| `narrative.Acceptance` as a list | 1 (`must be a string, got list`) |
| Item missing `status` | 1 |
| Item missing `title` | 1 |

`validateVbriefSchema` in `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.5` is what that command runs for JSON. For `--format json`, `--style scope` is unused. Required: info block (`xBRIEFInfo` or `vBRIEFInfo`) with version in `{0.6, 0.8}`; `plan.title`; `plan.status` in the plan-status enum; `plan.items` as an array; each item `title` and `status` (item enum includes `pending` and `auto`). `plan.id` is optional. `narrative` / `narratives` values, when present, must be strings. `plan.metadata` is an untyped object.

Other already-shipped shapes:

- Schema `xbrief/schemas/xbrief-core-0.8.schema.json`: Plan requires `title`, `status`, `items`; PlanItem requires `title`, `status`; `plan.id` optional with dotted-id pattern; item `effort` optional enum; narratives `additionalProperties: string`.
- `xbrief:create --style scope` (`styles.js` `buildStyleDocument`): empty `items`, default status `draft`, `metadata.kind: "scope"`.
- Lab 7 `lifecycle-lab.mjs` `story()`: empty `items`, `kind: "story"`, no swarm block. Both supplied lab scopes stay that shape; Task 5 is the first learner-authored file.
- Swarm-ready contract in `.deft/core/vbrief/vbrief.md`: `kind: "story"` plus `swarm.readiness: "ready"` is the concurrent-allocation gate (2-5 acceptance items, traces, non-empty `file_scope` / `verify_commands`). `needs_refinement` is explicit unreadiness.
- Later complete-gate evidence in `.deft/core/commands.md` (#3240 / #3305 / #1620): `plan.items[].x-directive/evidence` (typed object). Bare `evidence` keys fail conformance. String `narrative.Evidence` is a different field.
- Module 6 already publishes a two-surface table (verify vs comparison rubric) at lines 82-86. Lab 7 Task 5 recovery already says "Add the envelope from the Module 6 worksheet." `verify-module-6.mjs` does not lock the "worked solution" recovery phrase.

## Findings

### 1. sharpens-framing — Bind three identity layers on the specimen, not a verify-versus-conventional pair

**Evidence.** The issue's proposed fix asks to mark which fields `xbrief:verify` requires and which are conventional, and to "state the valid item status values for a proposed scope." The 0.119.5 probe shows the learner's `pending` + `Evidence` + `Traces` file exits 0, as does empty `items`, version `0.6`, and `running`. Module 6 lines 82-86 already name that verify does not prove version `0.8`, status `proposed`, observable acceptance, or traces. Schema item statuses include `draft`, `proposed`, `approved`, `pending`, `running`, `completed`, `blocked`, `failed`, `cancelled`, and `auto`.

**Failure mode.** A two-bucket legend still leaves the original pain: a learner cannot tell whether `pending` is a defect, a legal schema value, or a course convention. "Valid for a proposed scope" collapses schema membership, Lab 7 structural exit 0, the O6.2 rubric, and later swarm-ready / complete-gate rules.

**Disposition.** The annotated specimen can bind if each shown field is labeled with one of: schema-required (verify-enforced), schema-legal-optional, this-worksheet (O6.2 rubric), or later-gate (swarm-ready / `x-directive/evidence`). Item `pending` stays schema-legal; this worksheet can prefer item `proposed` to match `plan.status`. String `narrative.Traces` is the course home for the required trace; string `narrative.Evidence` is schema-legal and is a different field from `x-directive/evidence`. Keep the existing verify-versus-rubric table; the missing piece is a labeled document, not a second required-field list that disagrees with that table.

### 2. sharpens-framing — Put the labeled specimen on Module 6 Part B

**Evidence.** Module 4 lines 249-251 forbid treating the cards as complete JSON files. O4.1 inspects path-plus-field classification. Part B is the first authoring task; Lab 7 Task 5 already points recovery at "the Module 6 worksheet." `scripts/verify-module-6.mjs` requires the explained solution to contain exactly one schema-0.8 proposed JSON with two to five traced items.

**Failure mode.** A complete JSON specimen under Module 4 recuts that module's classification contract. A second JSON fence in the solution trips the "exactly one" lock. Leaving the specimen only in Module 4 leaves Lab 7's worksheet pointer empty.

**Disposition.** Land one labeled JSON fence (or a JSON fence plus a field-legend table) in Module 6 Part B / the worksheet the recovery row cites. Keep Module 4 on card-level facts. Keep the solution's two-item JSON as the complete worked artifact. Point Module 6 line 524 at that worksheet specimen. Lab 7's existing pointer then resolves.

### 3. sharpens-framing — Show field identity on a skeleton; keep Part B's two-to-five traced items as the rubric

**Evidence.** The issue's proposed "minimal" names the envelope plus one item with `narrative.Acceptance`. The walkthrough (Module 6 lines 322-324) also records "one item." Part B and O6.2 inspection require two to five traced acceptance criteria. The solution lock requires two to five items with both `Acceptance` and `Traces`. The one-item issue-body specimen exits 0 on verify, as does a zero-item file.

**Failure mode.** Publishing the one-item skeleton as the Part B reference teaches a verify-green file that still fails the rubric and the solution lock. Learners copy one `Acceptance` string and treat Lab 7 exit 0 as O6.2 complete.

**Disposition.** Caption the new fence as a field-identity skeleton. State on the same page that O6.2 still needs two to five items, each with a string `Acceptance` and a trace, `plan.status: proposed`, schema `0.8`, and the no-authority sentence. Align the walkthrough's "one item" line with that rubric on the same recut, or mark the walkthrough as a shaping sketch whose Part B count wins.

### 4. sharpens-framing — Keep create-defaults and solution extras off the required legend

**Evidence.** `xbrief:create --style scope` emits empty `items`, `status: draft`, and `metadata.kind: "scope"`. Lab 7 `story()` emits empty `items` and `kind: "story"` with no swarm block. The solution adds `effort`, `kind: "story"`, and a `swarm` object with `readiness: "needs_refinement"` and empty `verify_commands`. Verify accepts all of those files. `--style scope` on Lab 7's command is the create/verify P0 style flag; it is not `plan.metadata.kind`.

**Failure mode.** Copying the solution swarm block or `effort` onto the "minimal" specimen teaches concurrent-allocation metadata and effort estimates as ordinary proposed authoring. Copying create's empty `items` / `draft` / `kind: scope` teaches a legal create default that fails Part B. Equating CLI `--style scope` with `metadata.kind` mislabels story taxonomy.

**Disposition.** On the Part B skeleton: `plan.id` (worksheet story ID; optional for verify), `plan.title`, `plan.status: proposed`, one shown item with `title`, `status`, and string `narrative.Acceptance` plus `narrative.Traces`, and a legend that `effort` and `plan.metadata.kind` / `swarm` are optional for this proposed candidate. `kind: "story"` is the story-taxonomy value when present. Swarm-ready `readiness: "ready"` stays the later allocation contract. The solution may keep its `needs_refinement` block as unreadiness pedagogy in the answer key.

## Road not taken

Two other specimens were considered.

- Module 4 as the home for the JSON fence, because that is first contact with field names. That holds only if Module 4's "not complete JSON files" contract is deliberately recut and O4.1 gains a non-authoring specimen without becoming an authoring outcome. The authoring task and Lab 7 pointer already sit on Module 6.
- Shipping `xbrief:create --style scope` output as the reference, because it is the engine's generated scope document. That holds only if that default gained non-empty string `Acceptance` items and `proposed` status, and Module 6 were allowed that command. Today's default is empty `items` and `draft`, and Part B is command-free.

## Injection / swarm lens

The recut names identity of `plan.metadata.kind` and `swarm` on a proposed-scope teaching artifact. It does not change live authority, untrusted input, envelopes, worktrees, or shared state. The swarm-relevant miss is teaching allocation metadata as required proposed shape; finding 4 is that miss. Lab 7's supplied scopes and `xbrief:create` already omit `plan.metadata.swarm` on proposed candidates.

## Census

- `blocks-the-design`: none
- `sharpens-framing`: 4 (identity layers; Module 6 Part B placement; skeleton vs 2-5 rubric; optional extras / style-vs-kind)
- `footnote`: none

metadata.issueBody:
## Course context

Module 6 Part B, and Module 4 before it, taken in order by a mid/senior learner using only course material (Windows 11 ARM64). The Part B artifact is later checked by `xbrief:verify` in Lab 7 Task 5.

## What happened

Module 6 Part B asks me to **author a real schema-0.8 proposed-scope JSON file** that Lab 7 later structurally verifies. It must contain "one story ID and title", `plan.status: proposed`, 2–5 `plan.items[].narrative.Acceptance` criteria, and "expected static evidence and a trace back to the fictional idea for **every criterion**."

At that point, the course has shown no complete xBRIEF document:

- Module 4 ("xBRIEF as Durable State") teaches roles and names paths such as `plan.status`, `plan.items`, `plan.narratives`, and `planRef`, but contains no JSON example.
- The only full xBRIEF a learner has seen is the Lab 5 fixture `PROJECT-DEFINITION`, which has `"items": []`. It shows nothing about item shape.
- Module 6 never says **where** the story ID goes (`plan.id`? an item id?), what an item needs besides `narrative.Acceptance` (`id`, `title`, `status`?), which item `status` values are valid for a proposed scope, or where per-criterion evidence and traces live.
- Module 6 mentions `plan.metadata.swarm.depends_on` but never shows the `metadata` block.
- The module's own recovery table says: "`narrative.Acceptance must be a string, got list` … **Compare your item narrative with the worked solution**." In other words, the solution is the only template.

The worked solution then introduces keys and values the module never taught: `plan.narratives.Description` / `UserStory` / `Traces`, item `"status": "proposed"`, item `"effort"`, and a whole `plan.metadata` block with `kind: "story"` and `swarm.readiness / parallel_safe / file_scope / verify_commands / expected_outputs / depends_on`.

## Learner pain

I had to reverse-engineer the shape from an unrelated fixture and guess the placement of the ID, evidence, and traces. My first attempt used `plan.id`, item `status: "pending"`, and narrative keys `Evidence` and `Traces`. I cannot tell whether that shape is valid Directive practice or only happens to pass the minimal structural check. For an engineer who must "start developing software with Directive" afterwards, the most important hands-on authoring skill in the course, writing a scope, has no reference shape before the answer key.

## Reproduction

Complete Modules 4–6 in order, then try Module 6 Part B without opening the solution.

## Proposed fix

- Add a small annotated **minimal** scope xBRIEF to Module 4 or Module 6 (the envelope, `plan.id`/`title`/`status`/`narratives`, and one item with `id`/`title`/`status`/`narrative.Acceptance`). Mark which fields `xbrief:verify` requires and which are conventional.
- State the valid item `status` values for a proposed scope, and whether `plan.metadata.kind` / `swarm` are required, recommended, or optional for a story.
- Say explicitly where "expected evidence" and "trace" belong (for example, `narrative.Traces`), or say that they may live in the worksheet only.
- Change the recovery row so it points to that reference instead of the solution.
